categories.desc: Everyday ways to say something is getting to you. Safe almost anywhere.
cards: C'est agaçant.
It's irritating.
Neutral and fine anywhere. To say what it does to you: ça m'agace (‘it bugs me’), or in the past, ça m'a agacé(e).
Il me coupe la parole tout le temps, c'est agaçant.
He keeps interrupting me, it's irritating.
Ça m'énerve !
It drives me mad! / It gets on my nerves!
The everyday word for annoyance. Énerver means to irritate, not to make nervous; for that, use stresser.
Ça m'énerve quand les gens parlent fort au téléphone dans le train.
It drives me mad when people talk loudly on the phone on the train.
C'est pénible.
It's a pain.
Tiresome, wearing. Works for people too: il est pénible, celui-là !
Ces travaux tous les matins à sept heures, c'est pénible.
These roadworks every morning at seven, it's such a pain.
Ça me tape sur les nerfs.
It gets on my nerves.
Literally ‘it hits me on the nerves’. Same register as ça m'énerve, but more vivid. Of a person: tu me tapes sur les nerfs.
Ce bruit de perceuse me tape sur les nerfs.
That drilling noise is getting on my nerves.

categories.desc: Casual and blunt: for friends and family, not the boss.
cards: J'en ai marre !
I'm sick of it!
The go-to casual complaint. J'en ai marre de + noun or infinitive: j'en ai marre d'attendre.
J'en ai marre de cette pluie, ça fait deux semaines !
I'm sick of this rain, it's been two weeks!
J'en ai ras le bol !
I've had it up to here!
Literally ‘I'm full to the brim of the bowl’, often with a hand swept over the head. A notch stronger than j'en ai marre. The noun is hyphenated: le ras-le-bol.
J'en ai ras le bol de faire le ménage tout seul !
I've had it with doing all the housework on my own!
Ça me soûle.
It's doing my head in.
Soûler is literally ‘to get someone drunk’; here, to wear someone out. Soûle sounds like /sul/. Huge with younger speakers: tu me soûles !
Il me parle de son match depuis une heure, ça me soûle.
He's been going on about his match for an hour, it's doing my head in.
C'est chiant !
It's a pain in the neck!
Vulgar (from chier) but extremely common among friends. Also means ‘boring’: ce film est chiant. Polite version: c'est pénible.
Il faut tout refaire depuis le début ? C'est chiant !
We have to redo it all from scratch? What a pain!

categories.desc: Aimed straight at the person getting on your nerves.
cards: Tu m'énerves !
You're getting on my nerves!
Blunt but everyday between siblings, partners and friends. To someone you call vous, it's a real confrontation.
Arrête de toucher à mes affaires, tu m'énerves !
Stop touching my stuff, you're getting on my nerves!
Tu me casses les pieds !
You're being a pain!
Literally ‘you're breaking my feet’. Mild and familiar. A pest is un casse-pieds: quel casse-pieds !
Tu me casses les pieds avec tes questions !
You're driving me up the wall with your questions!
T'es sérieux, là ?
Are you serious right now?
Exasperation rather than disbelief: là (‘right now’) sharpens it. To a woman: t'es sérieuse ?
Tu as encore oublié les clés ? T'es sérieux, là ?
You forgot the keys again? Are you serious right now?
Pourquoi tu t'énerves ?
Why are you getting worked up?
S'énerver = to lose your temper. Often asked by the person causing it, which only makes things worse.
— Je te l'ai dit cent fois ! — Oh là, pourquoi tu t'énerves ?
— I've told you a hundred times! — Whoa, why are you getting worked up?
Pourquoi tu fais la gueule ?
Why are you sulking?
Faire la gueule = to sulk. Gueule /ɡœl/ is slang for ‘mug’, so it's informal; neutral: faire la tête.
— Pourquoi tu fais la gueule ? — Je fais pas la gueule !
— Why are you sulking? — I'm not sulking!

categories.desc: For the absurd, the unfair and the depressingly familiar.
cards: C'est n'importe quoi !
That's ridiculous! / What nonsense!
For anything absurd, unfair or badly done. Cut to n'importe quoi ! as a dismissive retort.
Quinze euros pour un café ? C'est n'importe quoi !
Fifteen euros for a coffee? That's ridiculous!
Allez, c'est reparti !
Here we go again!
Exasperated when the same problem or argument comes back. Said brightly, it just means ‘off we go again’.
Encore une panne d'ordinateur ? Allez, c'est reparti !
Another computer crash? Here we go again!
Qu'est-ce que c'est que ce bazar ?
What on earth is this mess?
Bazar = a mess or a commotion. For noise: qu'est-ce que c'est que ce raffut ? Casual: c'est quoi ce bazar ?
Je pars cinq minutes et… qu'est-ce que c'est que ce bazar ?
I leave for five minutes and… what on earth is this mess?
T'es de mauvaise foi !
You know that's not true!
Mauvaise foi = refusing to admit the obvious to win an argument. A constant accusation in French arguments; also c'est de la mauvaise foi.
— J'ai jamais dit ça ! — Si, tu l'as dit. T'es de mauvaise foi !
— I never said that! — Yes, you did. You know that's not true!
Je perds mon temps.
I'm wasting my time.
Giving up on a pointless effort or conversation. Aimed at someone: tu me fais perdre mon temps.
J'essaie de lui expliquer depuis une heure, je perds mon temps.
I've been trying to explain it to him for an hour, I'm wasting my time.

categories.desc: Drawing the line: stop it, quiet down, leave me alone.
cards: Ça suffit !
That's enough!
Stops an argument or behaviour on the spot; the classic parent's line. Stronger: ça suffit maintenant !
Ça suffit, vous deux ! Allez dans vos chambres.
That's enough, you two! Go to your rooms.
Arrête un peu !
Give it a rest! / Cut it out!
Un peu doesn't soften it here; it means ‘come on, enough’. To vous or several people: arrêtez un peu.
Arrête un peu de te plaindre, on est en vacances !
Give the complaining a rest, we're on holiday!
Ça commence à bien faire !
This is getting beyond a joke!
A warning that your patience is about to run out. Literally ‘it's starting to do well’, said with heavy irony.
Trois fois que tu arrives en retard cette semaine, ça commence à bien faire !
That's the third time you've been late this week, this is getting beyond a joke!
Chut !
Shh! / Hush!
The t is pronounced: /ʃyt/. Politer: un peu de silence, s'il vous plaît.
Chut ! Le bébé dort.
Shh! The baby's asleep.
Lâche-moi !
Leave me alone! / Get off my back!
Lâcher = to let go of. Jokier: lâche-moi les baskets ! Politer: laisse-moi tranquille.
Lâche-moi, je t'ai dit que je ferais la vaisselle plus tard !
Get off my back, I told you I'd do the dishes later!
